name: Microsoft Data Centre — Newport / Imperial Park, Wales

book_concentration.rationale: Two hyperscale buildings on a single 40-acre Imperial Park campus at the former Quinn Radiators site rather than a multi-site spread.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Campus is under construction with phase-one go-live expected late 2026; SSE is still reinforcing the high-voltage feed, so firm grid capacity is not yet evidenced as operational.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Part of a fast-growing South Wales M4 corridor cluster alongside Vantage CWL1 and other Imperial Park developments, sharing regional grid infrastructure.

trigger_gap.rationale: No disclosed availability or parametric curtailment cover; assumed damage-only property cover for a pre-operational hyperscale build.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: £2.5bn multi-year UK AI investment horizon against a campus still under construction with limited operating curtailment history.

data_monitoring.rationale: Hyperscaler with global fleet telemetry and on-site circular-centre operations for UK hardware lifecycle management.

product_fit.rationale: No disclosed availability or parametric curtailment insurance product for the Newport build.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Asset-level entity without dedicated insurance underwriting function.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Backed by Microsoft's balance sheet as part of its largest-ever UK investment programme.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Physical asset, not a risk-pricing or underwriting entity.

notes: Imperial Park brownfield campus; planning approved 2024; South Wales AI Growth Zone; SSE 1.94 km HV cable reinforcement in progress; part of £2.5bn UK AI DC programme.

name: Oracle Cloud — UK Sovereign Region (London & Newport)

book_concentration.rationale: Dual-region sovereign cloud split across geographically separate London and Newport facilities rather than one campus.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Both regions have been operational since 2019–2020 with N2 redundant power and generator backups documented for OCI facilities.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Two UK regions interconnected by private backbone but both sit on domestic grid boundaries, giving partial geographic diversification only.

trigger_gap.rationale: No disclosed availability or parametric curtailment insurance; sovereign SLA focus is on uptime rather than grid-firmness cover.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: Regions operating since 2019–2020 with long-term government workloads, but limited public curtailment-loss history.

data_monitoring.rationale: Hyperscale OCI platform with UK-based control, monitoring and logging systems under sovereign operations model.

product_fit.rationale: Engineering redundancy (UPS, generators) documented but no grid-availability insurance product disclosed.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Cloud region asset without dedicated insurance underwriting capability.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Oracle-backed sovereign infrastructure serving UK government and defence workloads with PASF-accredited facilities.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Infrastructure asset, not a risk-pricing entity.

notes: Dual-region UK Sovereign Cloud: London (Dec 2019) and Newport (Jul 2020); PASF-accredited; physically isolated rooms within UK colocation sites; inter-region private backbone.

name: Pure Data Centres — Park Royal, West London

book_concentration.rationale: Single 10-acre Park Royal campus (LON02) delivering up to 56–72 MW IT load in one West London availability-zone location.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Pure DC reports 70 MVA secured via a dedicated substation but construction is not due until 2026–2029 amid documented West London grid constraints.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Park Royal sits in the SSEN/UKPN West London demand cluster where data-centre load has absorbed remaining capacity through the 2030s.

trigger_gap.rationale: No disclosed availability or parametric curtailment cover for the pre-construction Park Royal JV.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: c.£1bn build with 2029 operations target against a short record of West London curtailment risk for this specific site.

data_monitoring.rationale: Developer with hyperscaler fit-out track record but no operational DCIM telemetry yet as site is pre-construction.

product_fit.rationale: Liquid-cooled AI-ready design planned but no insurance availability product disclosed.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Asset-level developer entity without underwriting function.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Oaktree-backed Pure DC in JV with FTSE-listed SEGRO on a c.£1bn fully fitted campus.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Physical asset under development, not a pricing entity.

notes: No Pure DC facility in Croydon identified; entity mapped to confirmed Park Royal (Premier Park) LON02 site. Planning approved; 70 MVA secured power; construction from 2026, ops targeted 2029. West London grid-constrained cluster.

name: BT Adastral Park — Martlesham / Ipswich DC Cluster

book_concentration.rationale: Single 100-acre campus hosting BT's main R&D site, Network Operations Centre and operational data-centre/server-room load (~11 MVA peak).

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Operational site with 11.5 MVA allocated capacity and 8 MW private-wire solar supplying up to 90% of summer demand, indicating largely firm grid connection.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Fed from UKPN Eastern 33 kV network linked to Cliff Quay/Felixstowe radial circuits, sharing regional reinforcement needs with port and housing growth.

trigger_gap.rationale: No disclosed availability or parametric curtailment insurance for telco operational DC load.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: Long-operating campus since 1975 but UKPN documents flag potential future load growth to 40 MVA with uncertain timing against grid reinforcement.

data_monitoring.rationale: Network Operations Centre and intelligent PDU power-down monitoring across operational kit rooms.

product_fit.rationale: 8 MW private-wire solar and on-site generation partially mitigate grid-import exposure but no insurance availability product.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Telco campus asset without dedicated insurance underwriting.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: BT Group plc balance sheet backing a nationally critical R&D and network-operations campus.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Operational asset, not a risk-pricing entity.

notes: BT main R&D and NOC campus; ~4,000 staff plus Innovation Martlesham cluster; majority of site power consumed by DC/server rooms; UKPN Martlesham Primary 11.5 MVA allocation; Brightwell 8 MW private-wire solar.

name: Bloomberg Data Centre — Greenwich View Place, London

book_concentration.rationale: Single dedicated 34,875 sq ft Isle of Dogs facility occupied by Bloomberg since the mid-1990s for data-centre and disaster-recovery operations.

non_firm_intensity.rationale: Fully operational data centre running an estimated 3.5 MVA load on a ten-year lease through 2029 with potential to 10 MVA.

aggregation_correlation.rationale: Located on the Greenwich View estate in Docklands alongside multiple neighbouring data-centre buildings sharing local power infrastructure.

trigger_gap.rationale: No disclosed availability or parametric curtailment cover; enterprise-owned DR site assumed damage-only.

tenor_mismatch.rationale: Long operating history since 1994 but lease reversion 2029 against evolving Docklands grid demand.

data_monitoring.rationale: Global financial data firm with DCIM standards across 100+ colocation sites and dedicated node-site infrastructure management.

product_fit.rationale: Dedicated DR facility but no grid-availability insurance product disclosed.

underwriting_expertise.rationale: Enterprise DC asset without insurance underwriting function.

capital_reinsurance.rationale: Bloomberg LP balance sheet; also uses Equinix colocation for additional London infrastructure.

pricing_modelling.rationale: Physical asset, not a pricing entity.

notes: 8 Greenwich View Place, Isle of Dogs; built 1988; ~3.5 MVA operating load (up to 10 MVA potential); lease to Sep 2029; complements Equinix colocation footprint.
